title: Couples mobile app built on the issue pipeline diagram
userDescription: Convert this diagram into a mobile app for couples where they can log issues, and they both see where they are in the "issue pipeline".  The app uses this pipeline to navigate individual issues.  It has two modes: issue raiser, issue causer. Either side can raise issues, and the app tracks issues. App would allow creation of Impact statements, all the places where documenting thoughts could occur, journaling, timers for each side speaking, etc.  MVP would include allowing the user to scroll through the diagram and see where they are in the conflict process.  Fully-encrypted user data.  Future expansion: Affiliated with therapy platforms, video chatting with therapists.  Related to the voice tracker idea I had that listens in to a couple's fight and flags when someone breaks any agreed-upon fight rules (name-calling, shutting down, stonewalling).
goal: - A user can scroll the diagram on a phone and see the current step marked
- Either person can raise an issue and both see it
- All user data is stored encrypted
- A written spec exists before any app code
- users use the clickable-ness of the diagram to navigate a conflict with their person.
notInScope: - Affiliation with therapy platforms; named as future expansion, no task yet
- Video chatting with therapists; named as future expansion, no task yet
- The voice tracker that listens to a fight and flags broken fight rules; a related separate idea, no task yet
problemSolvedByTask: Couples lose track of where they are in resolving an issue
description: Repo is currently a small Bun app (server.js + index.html) that lets a person view/edit mermaid `.mmd` flowcharts and trace one path through them; it has no user accounts, no data storage beyond the raw diagram text files, no auth, and no mobile packaging of any kind. diagrams/accountability.mmd is the "issue causer" accountability pipeline the user means by "issue pipeline" — nodes like SELF_CREATE_SYNTHETIC_IMPACT_STATEMENT, Q_THEIR_IMPACT_STATEMENT, and SELF_CHECK_EMPATHY_GOAL/SELF_CHECK_REGRET_GOAL/SELF_CHECK_FOLLOW_UP_GOAL already encode the impact-statement and empathy/regret/follow-up stages the request describes; diagrams/say-something-or-let-it-go.mmd and diagrams/stop-causing-harms.mmd are separate, smaller flowcharts in the same repo. index.html's parseEdges/walkTrail functions already do path-highlighting through a diagram in the browser, which is the closest existing building block to the requested MVP ("scroll through the diagram and see where you are"), but it runs in a desktop browser tab, not a mobile app, and has no concept of a second user, a raiser/causer role, or persisted per-couple state. The request asks for a native/mobile app, per-user encrypted data, two-role issue tracking, journaling, speaking timers, and (as future work) audio monitoring and therapist video chat — none of which has any code, chosen framework, backend, or auth/encryption library anywhere in this repo, so no concrete file list can be given without first deciding a mobile stack (e.g. React Native/Expo vs. native) and a backend, which the request does not specify. This is effectively a new product built on top of the diagram-viewing idea rather than a bounded change to the existing viewer.

title: Issue-raiser check-ins and decision-point break timer
userDescription: the issue-raiser side should be focused on asking "do you feel heard by your partner?" and "Do you feel your partner understands the issue and impact on you?".  one of the ways it answers these questions is by checking in with the issue-raiser as the couple navigates the diagram and works through decision points during the conflict.  Separately, the app monitors how long the couple has remained on a decision point and sets time limits so that it can ask "do you need to take a break from the discussion?"
chainGoal: - A couples app that walks both people through the issue pipeline diagram; tasks 1 and 2
- Task 1 builds the app and the issue-causer side; task 2 adds the issue-raiser check-ins and the break timer
goal: - The issue-raiser is asked "do you feel heard?" at check-in points
- The issue-raiser is asked "does your partner understand the issue and impact?"
- Time on a decision point is tracked and a limit triggers the break prompt
- A written spec covers this before any app code
notInScope: - The issue-causer side; task 1 owns it
- The full app build; task 1 owns it
- The voice tracker; separate idea, no task
problemSolvedByTask: The issue-raiser has no way to say they still feel unheard
description: index.html is the only place diagram interaction currently happens: parseEdges/walkTrail/highlightPath track a single chosenAnswers Set as a user clicks through Q_-prefixed decision nodes, with no concept of two people, roles, or elapsed time on a node. There is no "issue-raiser" vs "issue-causer" role anywhere in the code (diagrams/accountability.mmd is written entirely from one person's "Me" perspective) and no existing check-in, prompt, or timer UI to build on. Q_*-prefixed diamond nodes across diagrams/*.mmd are the natural existing mapping for "decision points." Delivering this needs: a role selector so the app knows who the issue-raiser is, a check-in prompt surfaced as walkTrail's active node advances, and a per-node timer (started when a node becomes the bright/active node in highlightPath) that fires a break-suggestion prompt once a configurable time limit is reached. None of the role, check-in, or timer concepts exist in server.js either, and this can be built as client-only state in index.html without server or diagram-file changes. .taskTools/tasks.json task 1 ("Couples mobile app...") is the umbrella idea that also expects raiser/causer roles and per-side timers, but this task can be scoped to the existing single-page web viewer instead of waiting on a mobile rebuild.
tests: Stay on one decision point past the limit, see the break prompt

blockedBy.reason: Task 1 builds the couples mobile app itself (spec, mobile framework/backend, issue-raiser/issue-causer modes, and diagram-navigation state tracking) and none of that exists yet in the repo (modifiableFiles is empty, readOnlyFiles is "*", no spec written). This task's check-in prompts and decision-point timers are features layered on top of that app's raiser mode and diagram-navigation state, so they have nothing to attach to until task 1 produces the app/spec.

chainGoal: - A couples app that walks both people through the issue pipeline diagram; tasks 1, 2, and 3

goal: - A check-in sends a phone notification at its time
- A scheduled loop-back time creates an event in the phone calendar
- Both partners get the reminder
- A written spec covers this before any app code
notInScope: - The check-in questions themselves; task 2 owns them
- The full app build; task 1 owns it
- Therapist scheduling; future idea, no task
problemSolvedByTask: Couples agree to come back to an issue and then forget
description: Repo has no mobile app yet: task 1 ("Couples mobile app...") and task 2 ("Issue-raiser check-ins and decision-point break timer") are both still open in .taskTools/tasks.json with modifiableFiles: [] and readOnlyFiles: "*", meaning no mobile framework, backend, check-in UI, or scheduling concept exists in code. index.html only implements a desktop-browser mermaid diagram viewer (parseEdges/walkTrail/highlightPath) with no user accounts, no persisted state, and no notification or calendar code anywhere in the repo. server.js is a Bun HTTP server exposing only diagram CRUD endpoints (/api/diagrams, /api/watch) with no auth, user, or scheduling model to attach reminders to. This request adds push notifications for check-ins (which task 2 has not built yet) and two-way calendar-reminder integration (device calendar or a service like Google/Apple Calendar) so scheduled items actually create reminders, but no mobile stack, push-notification service, or calendar API has been chosen anywhere in the repo. No concrete file list can be given without those choices first, so this is new functionality layered on two not-yet-built features (the mobile app and the check-in system) rather than a bounded change to the existing diagram viewer.
tests: Agree a loop-back time, see it land on the phone calendar and get a notification

blockedBy.reason: Notifications for check-ins need the check-in feature to exist first, and task 2 is what builds issue-raiser check-ins; this task only adds notifications and calendar-reminder integration on top of that.

title: Journals for the issue-raiser and note-taker, with photos of paper notes at close-out
userDescription: for the person who raises the issue, they are given a notepad to jot down their thoughts and ideas and whatnot, kind of like a journal entry for when they create the issue. for the take notes side, that person is given a similar journal but it is better to take notes with pen and paper so the option to take pictures of the notes as part of closing out the conflict should be added as a feature.
chainGoal: - A couples app that walks both people through the issue pipeline diagram; tasks 1, 2, 3, and the journal tasks
goal: - The issue-raiser can write a journal entry when creating the issue
- The note-taker has a journal for the same issue
- The note-taker can add photos of paper notes when closing out the conflict
- Journal entries and photos are stored encrypted
notInScope: - The full app build; task 1 owns it
- Reading text out of the photos; photos are stored as images
- Sharing journal entries with the partner; the share-entries task owns it
problemSolvedByTask: Both: thoughts get lost between raising an issue and working through it, and paper notes are better in the moments because they engage your frontal lobe, but get lost after
description: The app (index.html + server.js, a Bun-served Mermaid diagram viewer) has no per-role journaling feature today. diagrams/accountability.mmd defines RAISE_ISSUE ("Other side raises an issue") and SELF_TAKE_NOTES ("Me: take notes") as plain flowchart node labels only, with no attached UI or storage. server.js currently only exposes GET/PUT on /api/diagrams/:name (validated by isValidName) for .mmd text files, plus an SSE watch endpoint; it has no endpoint for freeform journal text or image uploads. index.html's #output/#diagram area renders the SVG and highlights the chosen-path trail via chosenAnswers, but has no notepad/journal panel tied to a node. Building this needs: a notepad UI for the issue-raiser, a similar journal UI for the note-taker, a photo-capture/upload control on the note-taker's journal for pictures of handwritten notes taken when closing out the conflict, and new server.js persistence (text notes plus image files) since none exists. Open design decisions: how notes/photos associate with a diagram session or node, where they are stored, and what UI action represents "closing out the conflict."
tests: Raise an issue, write a journal entry, and see it saved with the issue

description: Root cause confirmed: in index.html, the `.inspector-destination-row { display: flex; ... }` rule has no `:not([hidden])` guard, unlike the sibling rule `.inspector-grid:not([hidden]) { display: grid; ... }` a few lines above it, which already establishes the pattern for this exact problem. viewer.ts correctly sets `destinationRow.hidden = !hasDestination` for decision/question nodes, but the unguarded CSS `display: flex` beats the `[hidden]` attribute's UA-stylesheet `display: none`, so the row stays visible with an empty select. Fix is to add `:not([hidden])` to the `.inspector-destination-row` selector, mirroring `.inspector-grid`.

goal: - Selecting a static or choice node whose outgoing edge already points somewhere sets destinationSelect.value to that destination's id, not '' (Terminal)
- This works even when the real destination is currently excluded from the option list because its kind === 'choice'

notInScope: - The naming-convention heuristic that decides 'choice' vs 'block' kind (viewer.ts:570-574) is not reworked here, only how the destination dropdown handles its result
- The separate bug where the destination row stays visible for decision nodes is task #30
problemSolvedByTask: Destination dropdown lies about the graph
description: Confirmed root cause in viewer.ts: renderNodeInspector's destination-options loop (~line 1114-1117) skips any candidate node with kind === 'choice', so outgoingDestination(node.id, graph) can return an id that was never added as an <option>, leaving destinationSelect.value unmatched and silently defaulting to the 'Terminal' option (value ''). Node kind is assigned in the graph parser (viewer.ts ~line 570-574) by a naming-convention heuristic (id starts with fromId + '_' plus an unlabeled edge), not a reliable structural signal, so a real destination node can still be misclassified as 'choice'. Fix is to stop excluding kind === 'choice' candidates from the options loop (or otherwise guarantee the true destination always has a matching option) so destinationSelect.value correctly reflects outgoingDestination(node.id, graph).
tests: Load a diagram with a static/choice node that already has a real outgoing edge to an existing block, select that node, and assert destinationSelect.value equals the real destination's id (not '' / Terminal).

title: Fix shared edge-line parser to correctly handle a chained A --> B --> C on one line
userDescription: Bug: 'Insert static block before' doesn't splice into the graph.  Repro: Graph is `A --> B --> C`. I select `B`.  I choose `Insert static block before`. I expect: `A --> NEW --> B --> C`.  I see: `A --> B --> C` and `New --> B`, instead.
goal: - parseEditorEdgeLine/parseEditorToken correctly parse a single-line chained edge like `A --> B --> C` into all three nodes and both edges, instead of only capturing the first arrow
- Selecting B and choosing 'insert static block before' on that shape produces `A --> NEW --> B --> C`, with the old A-->B edge gone and B-->C untouched
- The rendered diagram shows only the correct, updated graph — not a leftover disconnected node alongside the old edges
- `npm test` passes
notInScope: - Fan-in / root-node insert-static-before cases are already covered by existing passing tests and are not touched
- The second, independent renderer parser path (render()'s parseEdges plus phone-mode chunking) is not fixed here unless it turns out to share this exact one-arrow-per-line bug
problemSolvedByTask: Insert-before silently corrupts the graph
description: Root cause confirmed: parseEditorEdgeLine/parseEditorToken in viewer.ts only capture one arrow per physical line, so a single-line chained edge like `A --> B --> C` mis-parses — it corrupts the middle node's label and silently drops the trailing node/edge from editorGraph()'s model entirely. This affects every editor action built on editorGraph(), not just insertStaticBefore, so fixing the shared parser is the root-cause fix rather than patching insertStaticBefore alone. Separately, render() in viewer.ts uses a second, independent parser (parseEdges) plus phone-mode chunking (sliceIds/siblingIds/leadInIds/chunkSource) to build the on-screen SVG; this path is decoupled from editorGraph()/codeBox.value and is a candidate for the rendered diagram visually lagging the true source even when the underlying mermaid text is correct — worth checking but not assumed to share the bug. Reproduce in the browser test harness (resetEditorFixture/clickNode/clickInspectorAction in tests/index.html.test.ts) with a plain single-predecessor/single-successor middle node under both edge-declaration styles (own-line declarations, and nodes declared inline on their first edge, as in diagrams/say-something-or-let-it-go.mmd), checking both codeBox.value and the rendered SVG DOM.
tests: Build a minimal diagram A --> B --> C, select B, click 'insert static block before', assert the resulting source is A --> NEW --> B --> C (old A-->B edge gone, B-->C untouched).

description: commitEditorSource (viewer.ts ~line 639-651) is the single save path that generates/replaces the header block on every write, before saveDiagram() PUTs the source to /api/diagrams/:name — server.js needs no changes, it just persists whatever text it's given. loadDiagram (viewer.ts ~line 1658-1666) fetches the .mmd text and assigns it straight to codeBox.value before resetEditorHistory/render; parsing the header and restoring lastSelectedNodeId (via selectEditorNode) and outputBox.scrollLeft/scrollTop belongs there. The graph parser already skips lines starting with '%%' in two places (viewer.ts editorGraph's isSkippable check, and render()'s separate parseEdges), both operating per-line after trim, so a multi-line %%%%==== fence is already invisible to both as long as every line inside it (including the %%%%==== markers) starts with %%, which holds for this format — verify rather than assume for this exact fence. Header goes at the END of the file, after the diagram body, since 'flowchart TD' must stay the first line.

title: Add 'Insert static block after' inspector action that correctly splices for choice and block nodes
userDescription: Feature: new button 'Insert static block after' for choice blocks and static blocks.  It should splice into the graph. Example: Graph is `A --> B --> C`. I select `B`. I choose `Insert static block after`. I expect: `A --> B --> NEW --> C`.
goal: - Selecting a static or choice node and choosing 'insert static block after' produces source --> NEW --> old-destination, with the old outgoing edge redirected to NEW rather than dropped
- The action is available in the inspector for both node.kind === 'choice' and node.kind === 'block'
- Inserting after a terminal node (no existing destination) just adds NEW as the new destination, same as today's 'add static block after' behavior for that case
- `npm test` passes
notInScope: - The existing legacy 'add-static-after' button, applyDestination(NEW_STATIC_DESTINATION), and commitNewStaticAfter are left untouched — this is a new, separate action, not a fix to the old one
- A parallel 'insert decision after' action is a separate task
- Task #32's shared single-line `A --> B --> C` chained-edge parser bug — this task's tests should not rely on that being fixed
problemSolvedByTask: No way to insert a block after mid-chain without losing the tail
description: commitNewStaticAfter (viewer.ts ~line 1158) creates a new static block and calls replaceOutgoing(sourceId, staticId, graph), which only repoints source's outgoing edge to the new block and drops the old destination — root cause of why the existing 'add-static-after' silently orphans the old successor. insertStaticBefore (viewer.ts ~line 756) is the mirror-direction reference: it captures predecessor edges, rewrites them to point at the new node, then adds one edge from the new node to the originally selected node. A new commit function (e.g. commitInsertStaticAfter) should follow that same shape in reverse: capture source's current outgoing destination via outgoingDestination(sourceId, graph) before rewriting, call replaceOutgoing(sourceId, staticId, graph) to point source at the new block, then append an edge from staticId to the captured old destination only if one existed. Wire a new 'insert-static-after' action into nodeInspectorActions for both node.kind === 'choice' (~line 1101-1105) and node.kind === 'block' (~line 1095-1100), and add its handler in the nodeInspectorActions click listener (~line 1306-1330) alongside the existing insert-static-before/insert-decision-before handlers.
tests: Build A --> B --> C, select B, click 'insert static block after', assert the result is A --> B --> NEW --> C (old B-->C edge gone, A-->B untouched). Repeat selecting a choice node.

title: Add 'Insert decision block after' inspector action with an asymmetric two-choice splice for choice and block nodes
userDescription: Feature: new button 'Insert decision block after' for choice blocks and static blocks.  It should splice into the graph.  Example: Graph is `A --> B --> C`. I select `B`.  I choose `Insert static block after`.  I expect: `A --> B --> Q_NEW --> Q_NEW_CHOICE_Y --> C`, and `Q_NEW --> Q_NEW_CHOICE_N`.
goal: - Selecting a static or choice node and choosing 'insert decision block after' produces source --> Q_NEW, with Q_NEW's first choice reconnected to source's old destination and a second choice added as a fresh terminal branch — the old destination is never dropped
- The action is available in the inspector for both node.kind === 'choice' and node.kind === 'block'
- Inserting after a terminal node (no existing destination) creates Q_NEW with two fresh terminal choices, matching the existing 'add Decision block after' behavior for that case
- `npm test` passes
notInScope: - The existing legacy 'add-decision-after' button and commitNewDecisionAfter (same drop-the-tail bug as commitNewStaticAfter) are left untouched — this is a new, separate action
- Task #34's 'insert static block after' is a separate sibling task, not depended on here
- Task #32's shared single-line `A --> B --> C` chained-edge parser bug — this task's tests should not rely on that being fixed
problemSolvedByTask: No way to branch mid-chain without losing the tail
description: viewer.ts holds three non-matching precedents: commitNewDecisionAfter (~line 1167-1175) uses replaceOutgoing(sourceId, decisionId, graph) to splice in Q_NEW with one choice, dropping the old destination (same bug as commitNewStaticAfter); insertDecisionBefore (~line 782-811) correctly preserves predecessors/successors via removedLineIndexes + preserveInlineDecl but only builds one leading choice, in the 'before' direction; addQuestionAfter (~line 698-732, bound only to the hidden/dead addQuestionAfterBtn, not reachable from nodeInspectorActions) builds a Yes/No choice pair but reconnects BOTH choices to every old successor, which is not the wanted asymmetric shape. The new action needs insertDecisionBefore's after-direction splice mechanics (successors collected from outgoing edges of selected, removedLineIndexes, preserveInlineDecl for inline declarations) combined with a Yes/No-style choice pair where only one new choice id (via choiceId(decisionId, suffix)) gets `--> successor` and the second choice gets no outgoing edge. Wire a new 'insert-decision-after' inspectorActionButton into the node.kind === 'choice' (~line 1101-1105) and node.kind === 'block' (~line 1095-1100) branches of renderNodeInspector's action list, and add its branch in the nodeInspectorActions click listener (~line 1306-1330) next to the insert-decision-before handler. tests/index.html.test.ts is the DOM-driven suite (via inspectorActions() and clickInspectorAction()) that already covers add-decision-after and insert-decision-before with this same helper pattern, and is where new coverage belongs.
tests: Build A --> B --> C, select B, click 'insert decision block after', assert the result has B --> Q_NEW, Q_NEW --> Q_NEW_CHOICE_Y --> C, and Q_NEW --> Q_NEW_CHOICE_N (a terminal second choice). Repeat selecting a choice node.
